text:
hao: hi all, first week checklist hiccup. cloned dotfiles, set up asdf + brew, installed python/node via asdf but my GUI IDE (JetBrains) terminal launches with the system python/node. iTerm and plain terminal are fine. any quick rule of thumb for where to put PATH/asdf init so gui apps pick it up?

liz: welcome! :wave: short: put PATH and asdf init in your login profile (~/.zprofile for zsh). GUI apps launched from the macOS UI inherit a different environment. putting it in .zprofile (not .zshrc) usually helps. also avoid expensive commands in .zprofile so app launch stays snappy.

hao: got it. i had everything in .zshrc. moved to .zprofile but still see /opt/homebrew/bin/node before ~/.asdf/shims in the IDE terminal. i checked `which -a node`. what's the safe ordering?

mike: ensure you export asdf shims before adding brew to PATH. example: 

  export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
  if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH"; fi
  . "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh"

then restart the IDE (fully quit) so it picks up the login profile. sometimes you need to launch the IDE from terminal once (`open -a "WebStorm"`) to inherit envs as a workaround.

hao: thanks. another small one: npm global installs try to write to /usr/local despite asdf. i made ~/.npmrc with prefix=${HOME}/.npm-global and added that bin to PATH but some CLI tools (like pnpm) still land in brew paths after a `brew install pnpm`. is it OK to keep brew for tooling and asdf for runtimes?

liz: yep that's the usual split: brew for system tools (git, openssl, cmake), asdf for language runtimes you pin. avoid mixing: uninstall brew node if you plan to use asdf node. using ~/.npmrc prefix is good to avoid sudo.

hao: great. quick direnv question: repo has .envrc that uses `layout node` and `use asdf` — on first `direnv allow` i got "use asdf: asdf not found" in non-login shells. i guess direnv runs before my shell init sometimes?

mike: direnv requires asdf available in PATH when it parses .envrc. ensure asdf init is in a file that non-login shells read (or make .zshrc source .zprofile early). alternative: in .envrc add a small fallback: `if [ -f "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh" ]; then source "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh"; fi` so direnv can call asdf even if shell init hasn't run yet.

hao: nice tip. last thing: JetBrains code runner tasks don't pick up .env.local. i added envFile in run config but still inconsistent for tests. any enterprise-y gotchas?

liz: many IDEs spawn processes from the app bundle which don't load shell profiles. two approaches: 1) use IDE's envFile / run config to point to .env.local 2) use direnv + enable the IDE to "Use shell environment" if the IDE supports it 3) for shared dev experience put non-secret env vars in a dotfiles sample or in a .env.template and add docs. we prefer direnv for per-project envs and adding a small note in the repo README for IDE configs.

dev-setup-bot: Welcome @hao! Helpful links: dotfiles repo https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles, onboarding checklist https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard. If you need help editing the link script to backup existing files, ping @dotfiles-admin.

hao: thanks everyone, will re-order PATH, add the small asdf source in .envrc, and try launching the IDE from terminal as a test. really helpful :raised_hands:
